scenario: A 60-year-old male with COPD, head injury, respiratory failure, C-spine immobilization, and pending COVID testing requires a difficult airway approach. Initial video laryngoscopy is unsuccessful, rescue ventilation becomes difficult, and definitive airway is ultimately achieved with cricothyrotomy.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Set up for RSI. He's GCS 6 and satting 80% on the non-rebreather, so he's not protecting his airway. Start bagging him to pre-oxygenate while we get the tube and drugs ready.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: RSI meds drawn up and ready, patient pre-oxygenated with BVM. Ready for intubation on your go.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Pushing RSI now, I'm going for the tube. Confirm placement with waveform capnography once I'm in.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Pre-oxygenated with BVM, RSI meds given. Ready for your intubation attempt.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Tube's in, but his sat is still 67% on the vent at FiO2 100%. Get me waveform capnography now and re-auscultate both lung fields — could this be esophageal or a right mainstem?

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Waveform capnography shows a good sustained ETCO2 tracing — tube's in the trachea, not esophageal. Breath sounds equal bilaterally, so no mainstem. Sat's now up to 90% on the vent, FiO2 100%, PEEP 5. HR 95, BP 105/68, sinus rhythm.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Tube's confirmed and his sat's up to 90%. Start a propofol infusion to keep him comfortable and synchronous on the vent.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: He's on a ventilator now and stable enough for me to ask you this: what happened right before he collapsed, and does he have any medical history, medications, or allergies I should know about?

messages.speaker: relative
messages.content: He has COPD. He takes Spiriva and Ventolin. No allergies that I know of.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start an inline salbutamol nebulizer through the vent circuit — he's a known COPD patient with likely bronchospasm and he's still only satting 90% on 100%.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Give him IV hydrocortisone for the COPD exacerbation — he's still only satting 92% on 100% oxygen despite the nebulizer.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Hydrocortisone is in.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: One more thing that helps me a lot: in the days before this, was he running any fever, coughing more, or bringing up more phlegm than usual?

messages.speaker: relative
messages.content: I'm not really sure. He seemed about the same to me, but I wasn't with him all the time.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Add an inline ipratropium nebulizer to the salbutamol through the vent circuit — he's still only satting 92% on 100%, let's get combined bronchodilation going.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Add an inline ipratropium nebulizer to the salbutamol through the vent circuit — he's still only satting 92% on 100%, let's get combined bronchodilation going.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Ipratropium is in and running now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Give me a fresh sat reading — is he trending up from that 93% after the combined nebs? And keep an eye on his pressure, he's 90/60 on the propofol.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Sat's holding at 93% on 100% FiO2, PEEP 5 — not really climbing yet. HR 103, BP 90/60, RR 12, temp 38. Pressure's stable for now on the propofol but I'm watching it.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: I need one thing from you: what inhalers or COPD medications does he take at home, and had he been using them regularly or had he run out recently?

messages.speaker: relative
messages.content: Like I said, he takes Spiriva and Ventolin. I think he was using them, but I honestly don't know if he ran out.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Let's give IV magnesium sulfate as an adjunct for the bronchospasm — he's still only 93% on 100% FiO2 after the combined nebs.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Magnesium sulfate is running now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Give me a fresh sat and pressure now that the magnesium's running — is he coming up off 93%, and is the BP holding on the propofol?
